summary: The recorded base reproduced stale-width top-k corruption on the assigned gfx950 GPU. The exact candidate derives score allocation width from live seq_lens when the caller snapshot is too small. Its registered regression and six independent block-boundary/output cases passed. This prevents the original undersized allocation even though the backend's stale metadata source remains observable through a warning.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: stale max_seqlen_k=64 differed from correctly sized max_seqlen_k=4096 in 163/1040 top-k elements; two non-undersizing boundary controls passed.
Candidate regression on the exact commit: stale/correct outputs matched an independent Torch reference and warning/boundary assertions passed (3 tests).

Six independent cases covered zero-width caller, a 128-to-129 block crossing, one-column-short at 4096, same rounded width, oversized caller, and both attention output plus top-k. Every stale/edge call exactly matched its correctly sized reference.

gpu_execution.evidence: Executed on one AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. Source import resolved to /job/repo/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/prefill/flash_with_topk_idx.py.

remaining_limitations: No native C++ or FlyDSL compiler source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The available architecture was AMD gfx950, not the reported NVIDIA GB200/SM100; CUDA compute-sanitizer, Xid 31, and CUDA-specific compiler/ISA behavior were not tested.
Only one GPU was assigned, so the production TP=4/NCCL watchdog failure and multi-node behavior were not reproduced.
MiniMax-M3 weights and the production mixed-chunk serving workload were unavailable; validation used deterministic kernel fixtures and does not establish model semantic accuracy.
The backend can still originate stale _max_seqlen_k metadata; the candidate safely enlarges the allocation and warns rather than eliminating that metadata divergence.
